gaps.claim: A call that could not be read is counted as the promise kept. `unreadable` is in neither `walls` nor `answered`, and the Inconclusive branch fires only when ALL THREE are unreadable -- so one TLS timeout (they had one at 20:55 on 2026-09-12) and the check concludes `passed` for a claim about three tools from two readings. Rule 8, in the direction that sends a vendor a pass.

Tonight's refusal covers the ledger and stops there. `audits/checks.json` cites 607 run ids and is read the same blind way: `_load(...).get('audited') or {}` turns an unreadable file into one citing nothing, and the prose fallback's `except OSError: continue` drops it too. A checks.json caught mid-write makes every record cited only by it a victim of --apply. The identical defect, one file over, left in place by the fix for it.

Its docstring still calls itself "the symmetric reading to `_free_cash`" and that stopped being true tonight. `_deployed` now reads their position status; `_free_cash` still reads the newest `after` row of our own orders, which a website close never writes. After the 2026-09-12 close the two legs of `affordable()` describe one event differently -- conservative today, but the docstring asserts a symmetry the code no longer has.

Only the literal `closed` releases money, and no position has ever been observed resolving -- measuring a resolve is still open in NEXT.md. If a resolved position reads `resolved`/`settled`/`expired`, it is counted against the 60% ceiling forever and every resolved card ratchets the ceiling down until the lab cannot order at all. Nothing fails; it quietly stops trading. Note `scripts/paper.py:567` already keys on the same word, so this is the repository's existing assumption rather than a new one.

The record half asserts what the fix makes trivially true: once the refusal fires `keep_set` returns every record as `unreadable`, so `victims()` is empty and the assertion holds for any implementation that keeps everything unconditionally. The capture half has a real discriminator (a sibling capture takes `witness`, so losing `kept` is a deletion); the record half has none.

The assertion goes red on 2026-09-15 while the contract is fully honoured. Line 1201 calls night_refill(rows=...) with no `now`, so backtests.best() uses datetime.now() and the fixture rows (at 2026-09-12T12:00Z, p=30, stale_after 3.0 days) fall out of the window. Reproduced: best(rows, limit=1) -> 1 row today, 0 rows at 2026-09-15T16:00Z. Every sibling in test_pipeline_backtests.py pins now=NOW; this one does not. tests/meta, so the red aborts every session.

The docstring's contract is that the night does not stop searching when the first queue empties, quantifying the defect as 'six ticks, twelve minutes of a fourteen-hour night'. The assertion asks only len(walked) > 30*4. Gate the refill on did['refills'] < 3 and the walk reaches 150 over seven ticks, then searches nothing for the remaining ~293: all three assertions stay green on a night that searched fourteen minutes of ten hours.

The name claims the road (a room opens from a whole Nexus answer, never from a basket of ours) and the brakes (affordable, paper only, nothing during a deep pass). The assertion measures neither: actions['promote'] is a stub that unconditionally returns {rooms:1, orders:1}, so a night_promote that opened a room from our own basket, skipped affordable and posted live would keep it green. The property is really held by test_pipeline_night_spend.py, which drives the real function. Same shape as A04 of 2026-09-12, ruled on in this file.

The contract is 'one card named in three answers is bought once'; the assertion len(sent) == len(set(sent)) is satisfied by sent == []. Any regression that places no order at all -- a _stake of 0.0, an affordable that refuses, an open_strategy that raises before the buy loop -- leaves the de-duplication it exists for unexercised. Non-vacuous today (book 100000 -> stake 2000 -> one order), so latent rather than live; every sibling in the file asserts on a non-empty sent.

The contract is a permanent pairing (a ceiling on a key nothing emits); the assertion compares CEILINGS against one machine's CURRENT sizes(), three keys of which are conditional. processes.py:384-432 emits evidence_mb only if <root>/evidence is a directory (gitignored since D3, absent in any clone), next_oldest_days only if NEXT.md has an open parseable item, memory_lines only if the memory index exists. Run against a clone-shaped root: dead == ['evidence_mb','next_oldest_days'] -> failed, while both ceilings are correctly paired.

The docstring names the broken-reader state as lenient < strict; the verdict fails on lenient <= strict. Measured now: lenient 200 (saturated), strict 153. The 47 malformed messages are history and the hook is fixed, so once 200 well-formed commits sit on top, lenient == strict == 200 and the check goes red with the reader working perfectly. The same branch also fires when _git returns '' on a non-zero exit -- a failed read reported as a broken reader, rule 8.

The contract is 'a read-only review writes nothing'; the assertion exercises one of the two areas with two instruments blind to where the other reads. main(['--deep-pass','all']) never reaches area_lab (review.py:156-233), which loads scripts/lab.py and calls graded_pairs(), qa.lab.load, qa.rooms.load and five diary readers. Every diary it touches is gitignored, so git status cannot see a write, and the mtime snapshot covers only audits/. Today --lab appends a row to state/backtests.jsonl on every run and the check stays green.

The silence half is asserted on a fixture where the mechanism cannot load. reminders.py:37-38 returns 0 when scripts/processes.py is absent, and the 'quiet' subprocess runs against a tmp_path without it -- so the empty stdout proves the early return, not that reminders() is quiet. The second subprocess does load it, prints 'Tydenni ohlednuti nikdy neprobehl', and only returncode == 0 is asserted. Set MISSED_NIGHT_HOURS = 0 and both assertions still hold.

The docstring names a defect in patrol(since=...); the assertion drives within() and runs_from_records() in isolation and never calls patrol. Change processes.py:520 from runs_from_records(within(stamps, since)) to runs_from_records(stamps) -- the exact regression described -- and the test stays green because it calls within itself. The fixture writes tmp_path/scripts/quiet.py and tmp_path/state/nexus.jsonl and never passes tmp_path to anything that reads them.

Docstring: 'Five diaries, one window'. The assertion exercises two. It passes diaries=lambda name: [], so the _within wrappers on asked, answered, gave_up, backtests and orders (review.py:223-231) all filter empty lists; only lab.jsonl sessions and rooms.jsonl rows are measured. Drop _within from line 229 and the retrospective reports every backtest ever run under a 'last 7 days' heading, still green.

The docstring pins the vocabulary THIS READER depends on against the data; the assertion pins only the data, with the reader's vocabulary as a literal in the test. It reads state/nexus.jsonl and never reads review.area_lab. Revert review.py:223-228 to the historical type == 'ask' and the check stays green while the retrospective again prints '0 otazek Nexusovi' -- the incident the docstring cites.

The docstring claims '#97, exactly' -- that the watcher would have announced the fix -- but the assertion drives surface.fields_drift, which no production path calls (grep returns qa/surface.py:180 and three lines of this test). The reminder path is processes.surface_drift -> drift_against -> shape_drift, whose criterion is stricter: a field counts as appeared only if it is in now['always'] (in EVERY 2xx capture of that call in 48h). A field present in some answers is `appeared` here and silent in the mechanism.

The contract is that a summary excluding a population it holds must say so and say where it can be read; the assertion accepts that statement only from `counters_do_not_cover`. An exclusion stated inside `counters_cover` is thrown away by the NEGATIONS filter and reported as an absence. Reproduced: accounts_for({counters_cover: '...event-card bull/bear positions are not counted here, see /api/v1/event-cards/positions', counters_do_not_cover: []}) -> None -> verdict failed, with a reason that is false of the body it just read. #83's shape on the same endpoint, which cost a retraction.

The contract is 'a route their server serves is a route their documents name'; the assertion compares a path rewritten with the literal `{instance_id}` against their `paths` keys, so the real claim is '...under that exact parameter name'. Rename the parameter to `{clone_id}` in openapi -- a documentation-only change -- and served_but_undocumented reports a route they do document. Latent today.

The docstring's contract is one flow -- an agent that can clone a bot can fund it -- but the assertion fails on ANY authenticated /api/v1/cloned-bots operation that does not publish x-api-key. If they fix fund and document DELETE with `authorization` only (a legitimate user-only operation), credential_gap still returns a refusal and verdict is failed. The reason string hedges; the verdict does not, and the verdict is what moves the CHECK axis and what verify.py sends. This row is OPEN and filed as #89/#98.
DUPLICATE of R01 -- found independently by an auditor who had not seen the review. Judged as R01.

The docstring's contract is 'every cited id is in the COMMITTED manifest', and the journal and ledger are read from HEAD for exactly that reason (lines 126-127) -- but manifest.read() reads audits/evidence-manifest.jsonl in the WORKING TREE. A fold cites a new capture, the ledger is committed with the hook not running (--no-verify, or a clone with no core.hooksPath -- the case step 0 of the deep pass exists to repair), and the citation is in HEAD while its manifest line is only on disk: guard green, clone holds no proof.

The extractor re.findall(r'\bf\.([a-z_]+)\b') cannot match a camelCase or digit-bearing property, so a whole class of undefined reads is outside the population compared. Verified: over 'draw(f.displayState); x(f.a2a_id); y(f.title)' it returns ['title'] alone. The identical defect (P13) was fixed in the sibling guard in test_pipeline_rooms.py on 2026-09-11 by widening to [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

_next_items() wraps the whole read in `except Exception: return set()`, so a read it could not make is scored as a NEXT.md carrying nothing, and every entry of the pass's `next` list is then reported as missing. A failed read rendered as an empty read -- rule 8 -- in the file whose red step 9 reverts a night over. Low confidence from the auditor.
